## Manuscript title

Common decline, divergent endpoints: hierarchical demography across Antarctic penguin breeding islands

**Character count including spaces:** 102

## Abstract

Seabird breeding islands separate a marine trophic environment from discrete terrestrial reproductive patches, providing a tractable system for asking whether demographic state and temporal buffering occur at the same spatial scale. We analysed a complete 1991–2017 annual census of five neighbouring Adélie penguin (Pygoscelis adeliae) islands near Palmer Station, West Antarctic Peninsula, together with broader breeding-site records and independent spatial reconstruction from Torgersen Island. The five populations shared a strong long-term decline (PC1 of standardized log abundance = 96.4%) while annual growth was only moderately synchronized (median pairwise r = 0.373); this contrast is treated as established timescale-dependent context. We then partitioned temporal variability across nested census units. Among the three islands with unchanged colony-code rosters through 1991–2017, raw-abundance beta variability was 1.0737 from colony-code breeding components to islands but only 1.0112 from islands to the archipelago; 86.4% of the total log-beta transition occurred within islands. The ordering persisted before Litchfield extinction and after removing Litchfield entirely, and every eligible island retained greater within-island than among-island beta variability after linear detrending and for annual log growth. Local endpoints nevertheless diverged, including extinction, low-abundance persistence and contrasting regional replacement trajectories. Effective colony number retained a small positive conditional association with next-year growth (+0.1168). The coefficient remained +0.1126 after conditioning on growth over the preceding two annual intervals (96.4% of the original effect) and remained unusual under the same full-series circular-shift nulls (100,000 shifts: p = 0.00102; exact covariance-preserving shifts: 5/416, p = 0.0120). Its incremental held-out MSE gain, however, fell to +0.000444 and the original gain was compatible with synchronized year-block permutation noise (p = 0.262), supporting association rather than prediction or causality. Prospectively bounded sea-ice-duration and snowfall × habitat formulations were not supported. Independent Torgersen mapping documented habitat-structured attrition from 23 historic active subcolonies to five active footprints by 2022. The resulting hierarchy is asymmetric: islands retain distinct demographic states and endpoints, whereas most detectable temporal compensation resides among breeding components within islands.

## Open Research Statement

The primary Palmer Station Antarctica Long Term Ecological Research Adélie penguin census is publicly available at DOI 10.6073/pasta/89dd52217ca37e3a72a67f7a9bc3c82e. The sea-ice and Palmer Station weather data used in the bounded mechanism tests are publicly available at DOI 10.6073/pasta/4207e529832840db2282498d9f4f4f05 and DOI 10.6073/pasta/3eefb45dbfb784c3cabe3690ea46fe9e, respectively; broader APBP/MAPPPD data are publicly available as cited in the manuscript. Novel analysis code, frozen endpoint contracts, and result receipts used for this submission are publicly accessible for peer review at https://github.com/zuizui0223/mina. If the manuscript is accepted, the exact version of record of the analysis code and derived outputs will be archived in a permanent repository with a DOI, and the final Open Research Statement will be updated with that identifier.

## AI-use disclosure for the manuscript submission form

OpenAI ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol) was used during analysis and manuscript development to assist with code drafting and review, statistical sensitivity-analysis scripting, literature searching, and editorial drafting. All analyses were executed from version-controlled code, numerical results were checked against frozen result receipts, cited literature was independently verified, and the authors remain responsible for all analyses, interpretations, and text.

ESA requires the same AI use to be disclosed in the manuscript section to which it pertains and again in the Acknowledgments. The Word builder inserts both disclosures. If any AI tools beyond OpenAI ChatGPT were used, the final author-controlled metadata file must add them before submission.

## Dual Publication / overlap field

**AUTHOR CONFIRMATION REQUIRED.** ScholarOne requires disclosure of any overlap in data, text, or figures with work that is published, in press, submitted, or soon to be submitted elsewhere.

If—and only if—all authors confirm there is no relevant overlap, use:

> No overlapping manuscript is published, in press, submitted, or under review elsewhere, and no other manuscript using substantially overlapping data, text, or figures is currently planned for submission.

If overlap exists, replace that sentence with a factual description and upload the overlapping paper(s) as required by the journal; also explain the overlap in the cover letter.
